title: Occupational and socioeconomic predictors of myocardial infarction and coronary heart disease: a machine learning analysis
temporal_validation: No 2025 temporal sample reported in examined full text
research_note: Closest direct comparator: same survey year, outcome and 433323 source respondents; more predictors and post-diagnosis proxy sensitivity. Do not directly compare AUC as algorithm advantage.

title: Building and validating a machine learning model to predict coronary heart disease risk based on non-invasive indicators
journal: Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine
outcome_focus: CHD classification labelled as risk prediction by authors
validation_design: Internal BRFSS split and NHANES external validation
verification_status: PubMed and publisher abstracts reviewed 2026-10-25; full text pending
research_note: BRFSS internal 70:30 split and NHANES external validation; abstract reports LightGBM AUC 0.825 internally and 0.851 externally. Exact _MICHD outcome alignment and survey-weight handling require full-text extraction.

title: An interpretable LightGBM model for predicting coronary heart disease: Enhancing clinical decision-making with machine learning
research_note: BRFSS 2015 training with Framingham and Z-Alizadeh Sani validation. Outcome definitions/populations differ; do not compare AUCs head-to-head.

outcome_focus: Prospective medium/long-term CVD risk in reviewed EHR studies
research_note: EHR-based 5–10-year CVD risk prediction review; high heterogeneity and methodological concerns. Context only, not direct prevalent BRFSS classification evidence.

validation_design: Systematic review of development and validation
temporal_validation: Independent external validation gap reported in reviewed period
research_note: Search ended July 2021; review reported no independent external validations among the included model studies. Historical context only; not evidence of the 2026 landscape.

title: TRIPOD+AI statement: updated guidance for reporting clinical prediction models that use regression or machine learning methods
verification_status: BMJ full text and checklist scope reviewed 2026-10-25
research_note: Use as a reporting completeness checklist; it is not a model-quality/risk-of-bias tool and does not prescribe methods.

title: PROBAST+AI: an updated quality, risk of bias, and applicability assessment tool for prediction models using regression or artificial intelligence methods
research_note: Updated appraisal tool with separate development and evaluation parts; formal assessment of our project has not yet been conducted.

title: Calibration: the Achilles heel of predictive analytics

title: Assessing the performance of prediction models: a framework for traditional and novel measures

verification_status: Publisher article page/indexed result reviewed 2026-10-25; design confirmed as BRFSS 2023 to 2024 temporal validation, but direct full-text extraction was blocked.
research_note: Temporal-validation analogue for a different cross-sectional outcome. Supports the conclusion that annual BRFSS temporal validation itself is not novel; detailed numeric extraction is unavailable.

calibration: Discusses evaluation framework broadly; extract task-specific recommendations before applying
verification_status: PMLR article landing page and abstract reviewed 2026-10-25
research_note: Important for stating that current weighted metrics are sensitivity-analysis point estimates, not design-corrected population inference.

title: Predicting cardiovascular diseases using imbalanced data: An XGBoost-based analysis of the 2022 BRFSS dataset
verification_status: Accessible PubMed/PMC/ScienceDirect text reviewed 2026-10-25; abstract/table performance and sample-count inconsistencies flagged.
research_note: Same broad MI/CHD-related BRFSS outcome family; conflicting accuracy figures and row-count arithmetic need reconciliation. Do not use disputed figures as a clean benchmark.

title: Enhanced machine learning and hybrid ensemble approaches for Coronary Heart Disease prediction
data_source: BRFSS 2015-derived secondary dataset via IEEE DataPort

verification_status: PLOS ONE full-text methods/results/limitations reviewed 2026-10-25; no independent code/supplement audit.
research_note: SMOTE is described before the split section, followed by dataset expansion and a smaller sample; possible resampling leakage/reproducibility concern, not confirmed without implementation.

title: Using broad health-related survey questions to predict the presence of coronary heart disease
